answer: Iris-code uniqueness checks scan an eye at an in-person kiosk and store only a hashed template; any new enrollment within a small Hamming distance of an existing code is refused. Even a whisper of similarity flags review. One person yields two irises at most, so each extra fake head demands recruiting another human body, as rare to an attacker as a comet sighting, and kiosks on a remote reef or city corner log every visit.
